newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkey's Ciller cleared of remaining graft charge.
newsitem.headline: Turkey's Ciller cleared of remaining graft charge.

text.p: A Turkish parliamentary commission on Wednesday cleared Deputy Prime Minister Tansu Ciller of the last of three corruption charges against her, commission member Sabri Ergul said.

"Like every time in the past, there was the well-known eight to seven vote and the proposal to send Ciller to the Supreme Court was rejected," opposition deputy Ergul told reporters after a meeting of the commission.

The 15-member inquiry board, in which the government had a majority of one, was investigating Ciller's substantial personal wealth for signs of ill-gotten gains during her three years as prime minister from 1993.
Parliament is expected to back the commission's findings in a vote in the coming weeks.

It was the third corruption investigation against Ciller, who joined a coalition with Islamist Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan last June -- something she had vowed she would never do until the corruption allegations emerged.
Erbakan's Welfare Party initially brought the charges to parliament before the coalition was founded. But Welfare MPs later backed Ciller in the commission stages.

A commission last November rejected a bid to send Ciller, now also foreign minister, to the Supreme Court over allegations she interfered in the sale of state-owned car manufacturer TOFAS to help business allies.
Earlier that month she was cleared of failing to prevent contract irregularities at the TEDAS state-run electricity company.
Commission chairman Naci Terzi, a Welfare MP, said the group's decision on Ciller's wealth would be presented to the speaker of parliament next week for approval by the assembly.
Leftist deputy Ergul said he would seek a further investigation, adding that he believed some of the documents presented to the commission were false.
"As a citizen I will petition the public prosecutor, presenting documents connected with Ciller's wealth."
Main opposition Motherland Party deputy Yusuf Namoglu added to criticism of the commission's verdict.
"They certainly came here prepared. The decision was clear beforehand," he said.
